title: Obama Presidential Library: USAID Telecommunications Development & Infrastructure Security in Georgia and Armenia (2011–2012)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Obama Presidential Library: USAID Telecommunications Development & Infrastructure Security in Georgia and Armenia (2011–2012)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I. Request Scope & Description of Records

I request copies of all records created, received, or maintained within National Security Council (NSC) channels, or transmitted to/from NSC staff by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) or its Bureau for Europe and Eurasia (E&E), between April 6, 2011, and December 31, 2012, concerning telecommunications development, critical infrastructure security, and internet connectivity in Georgia and Armenia following the April 6, 2011, fiber-optic line severance outside Tbilisi.

For context, an elderly woman collecting copper in the hills outside of Tbilisi in April of 2011 disabled Armenia's internet connectivity:
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2011/apr/06/georgian-woman-cuts-web-access

Specifically, this request includes:

● NSC briefing memoranda, situation reports, and correspondence discussing the April 2011 fiber-optic severance and its effect on Armenian internet connectivity.

● Correspondence between NSC staff (e.g., the Senior Director for Russian and Eurasian Affairs) and USAID's Bureau for Europe and Eurasia regarding telecommunications sector resilience, broadband access, or critical infrastructure security in Georgia and Armenia.

● Interagency or bilateral correspondence discussing regional reliance on single-channel transit corridors (such as Armenian routes transiting Georgia or Iran).

● Any records reflecting U.S. Embassy Tbilisi or U.S. Embassy Yerevan reporting on the incident that was forwarded to or discussed within NSC channels.

II. Suggested Search Terms & Parameters

To assist your search, please query electronic and paper systems (including text collections, briefing books, and email databases) using the following keyword clusters:
● "USAID Georgia" OR "USAID Armenia"
● "Hayastan Shakarian" OR "ჰაიასტან შაქარიანი" OR "Հայաստան Շաքարյան"
● "telecommunications infrastructure" OR "Georgian telecommunications infrastructure" OR "Armenian telecommunications infrastructure" OR "South Caucasus telecommunications infrastructure"
● "broadband accessibility" OR "digital connectivity"
● "network security" OR critical "infrastructure protection"
● "Caucasus Online" OR "fiber optic" OR "internet blackout"


III. Date Range

The records sought span from April 6, 2011, through December 31, 2012.

IV. Format Request

I request that any responsive records be provided electronically via email or on digital storage media or, ideally, simply uploaded online in the spirit of the Obama library's "digital-first" ethos. 

V. Withholdings & Segregability

If any portion of this request is denied or withheld pursuant to statutory exemptions under the FOIA or Presidential Records Act, please specify the exemption(s) applied to each withheld record, provide a Vaughn index itemizing the basis for each withholding, and release all reasonably segregable, non-exempt portions. 

Thank you for your assistance with this request. I look forward to receiving your response within the statutory time frame. I appreciate the work that the Obama Presidential Library does each and every day.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

title: King County Medical Examiner's Office: Unidentified Decedent Case No. 87-624 ("Mediterranean Doe")

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Washington State Public Records Act (RCW 42.56), I am requesting access to and copies of all public records maintained by the King County Medical Examiner's Office (KCMEO) pertaining to Case Number 87-624.

Case Summary & Identifying Details:

- KCMEO Case Number: 87-624
- Date Found: June 15, 1987
- Location Found: Washington Ship Canal, west of the Aurora Bridge, Seattle, WA
- Subject: Unidentified white male, estimated age 30–40, ~5'8", ~180 lbs, thick eyebrows, Mediterranean appearance; found wearing a blue long-sleeve Monte Carlo shirt, black Jon Peters trousers with black belt and yellow metal buckle, dark-brown socks, and mahogany Florsheim dress shoes, size 9E.

Requested Records:

1. Investigation Reports & Case Files: Investigative notes, police liaison logs, personal effects inventories, clothing recovery sheets, and scene summaries.

2. Medical Examiner / Post-Mortem Records: I understand that autopsy and postmortem reports are confidential under RCW 68.50.105 except to the enumerated persons listed in that statute (family members, attending physician, prosecuting attorney/law enforcement, public health officials). This case has no identified next of kin. Please advise whether KCMEO exercises discretion to release the autopsy/postmortem report,
or the non-medical administrative portions of it, in cases where no next of kin has ever been identified — and, if the office declines to do so, please identify the specific statutory basis for withholding, consistent with RCW 42.56.210(3).

3. Biometric & Identification Records: Fingerprint cards, dental charts/records, post-mortem photographs or sketches, and any records concerning DNA sampling or profile submission (CODIS, NamUs, or outside forensic labs)

4. WSP Unidentified Persons Reporting: Records reflecting whether fingerprint, dental, or DNA data on this decedent was recorded and furnished to the Washington State Patrol's Missing and Unidentified Persons Unit under RCW 43.43.770, and any correspondence concerning the results of that submission.

5. Current Case Status: Records reflecting the current administrative status of Case #87-624 — whether the decedent has since been identified, whether remains were released or interred, or whether the case remains an open unidentified-decedent investigation.

Public Interest Statement:

I am an independent researcher investigating historical unidentified-decedent cases in King County. My purpose is to determine whether Case #87-624 remains open, whether biometric markers were preserved and are available for entry into modern databases, and whether the case was resolved historically without a public listing update. I understand the PRA does not require me to state a purpose, and offer this only for context.

Discussion about this case online shows confusion as to whether or not it is active or not:

Reddit thread:
https://www.reddit.com/r/UnresolvedMysteries/comments/m8yiev/mediterranean_john_doe_seattle_wa/

Websleuth's thread:
https://websleuths.com/threads/wa-seattle-whtmale-30-40-369umwa-found-floating-in-lake-washington-ship-canal-jun-87.681565/

Doe Network page:
https://www.doenetwork.org/cases/software/main.html?id=369umwa

Archived Seattle PI article describing case as active in 2008:
https://web.archive.org/web/20080506040218/http://seattlepi.nwsource.com/missing/noname.asp?county=king

Thank you for the work that the King County Medical Examiner's Office does every day. Thank you also for the commitment to transparency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
